**This vignette gives you a 1-minute summary of how to install and use the *Entropy* package for gene expression entropy estimation in Seurat objects and AnnData files. For more detailed workflows, check out the other vignettes.**

## Install the packages

### Stable version: *Entropy*

Installing our *Entropy* packages is easy. Just execute the following line into *R*:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(devtools)
devtools::install_github("ZauggGroup/entropy_package", force = TRUE)
```

If you receive an error message, make sure you installed the devtools package. If you don't have it installed yet, just execute the following code into *R*:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("devtools")
```

### Recommended for depth correction: *scuttle*

If you plan to use depth correction (`depth_correct = TRUE`, or
`entropy_depth_select()`), install the Bioconductor package *scuttle* first:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("scuttle")
```

*Entropy* uses `scuttle::downsampleMatrix()` to thin counts when it is
available. Without it, a built-in R sampler is used and a warning is logged.
Both draw counts without replacement. Before version 0.7.1 the built-in
sampler read every cell one column at a time, which took hours on datasets of
around 100,000 cells. If you are on an older version, install *scuttle*.

## Python and AnnData users

Python and Scanpy users can compute entropy directly from an `.h5ad` file and
join the result back into `adata.obs`. See the
[Python and AnnData workflow](python_anndata_workflow.html) for the complete
setup and examples.

Before choosing whether to thin counts, read
[Choosing depth correction](choosing_depth_correction.html) for the frontier,
retention weight, and automatic Seurat depth-selection workflow.
